title: Launch traffic timebox and emergency rollforward policy for runtime + console + API increments
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Summary: Define and document a coordinated traffic timebox and emergency rollforward policy for cross-surface (runtime, Console, and public API) incremental releases. Goal is to minimize blast radius during canary windows while enabling a clear, actionable path to roll forward a change when rollback is more harmful than progressing.

Why: Several recent rollbacks were driven by noisy downstream metrics and manual decisions with inconsistent criteria across teams. We need a single, operational policy that:
- Specifies timeboxed canary traffic allocations by tier (internal, beta customers, production cohorts)
- Defines deterministic health signals and thresholds for rollback vs rollforward decisions (latency P50/P95/SLO error budget, error rates, model quality regressions, infra OOMs)
- Documents the emergency rollforward gating criteria and the exact steps and owners for performing a rollforward when necessary (who authorizes, who performs, observability checks post-action)

Scope: Runtime serving changes, Console UI changes that affect traffic shaping or rollout signals, and API schema/behavior changes that are released via the same deployment windows. This policy will be incorporated into the launch runbook and preflight checklist and represented in the release train scheduler.

Outcomes:
- A one-page operational policy and a 10-step runbook annexed to each release ticket.
- Template traffic timebox allocations for canary cohorts and a mapping to Console flags and runtime routing rules.
- A list of deterministic monitoring signals (and their owners) that feed the decision matrix.
- Automation suggestions for enforcing timeboxes and initiating automated fallbacks where safe.

Constraints/trade-offs:
- Stricter timeboxes reduce detection time but can increase false positives and premature rollbacks. We prefer conservative timeboxes for high-risk runtime changes and longer observation windows for low-risk console copy/UX changes.
- Rollforward is riskier in that it accepts an imperfect patch forward; to mitigate, rollforward must be scoped, staged, and accompanied by immediate remediation playbooks.

Stakeholders:
- PM: Priya Nair (policy owner)
- Eng: Marcus Chen (execution owner), Sarah Lin (runtime), Diego Alvarez (routing), Elena Petrova (console)
- SRE/Oncall: Oncall rotation leads and Observability team (dashboards)

Next steps:
1) Workshop with runtime + console + SRE to finalize monitoring signals (by 2026-03-01) - DONE
2) Draft one-page policy and runbook (this ticket) - IN PROGRESS
3) Internal review with Eng Leads and Oncall (target 2026-03-15)
4) Pilot policy on next minor runtime release window (target 2026-03-25)
5) Iterate based on pilot and fold into release train orchestration templates (due 2026-04-01)
